articles.title: Selling 3D print files as downloads: the model that has to survive someone else's slicer
articles.excerpt: Selling 3D print files as downloads: the model that has to survive someone else's slicer Most downloads are finished when the buyer opens them. A 3D print file is barely started. Between your model an…
articles.body: Selling 3D print files as downloads: the model that has to survive someone else's slicer Most downloads are finished when the buyer opens them. A 3D print file is barely started. Between your model and the object on the buyer's shelf sit a slicer you did not choose, a printer you have never seen, a material you did not specify, and settings the buyer picked at midnight. When the print fails — and some prints always fail — the buyer does not blame the midnight settings. They blame the file, because the file is the only part of the chain with your name on it. Selling print files well means designing the delivery for everything that happens after the download, on machines you will never touch. The file is not the print A buyer is not really purchasing geometry.
articles.author: FileFreight

articles.title: Why `await Promise.all()` Can Crash Your Database (And How to Throttle Concurrent Async Tasks in Node.js)
articles.excerpt: It's the most natural-looking line in modern JavaScript: await Promise.all(ids.map((id) => processOrder(id))); Fast, concise, parallel. In development with 20 IDs it finishes in a blink. Then a backfi…
articles.body: It's the most natural-looking line in modern JavaScript: await Promise . all ( ids . map (( id ) => processOrder ( id ))); Fast, concise, parallel. In development with 20 IDs it finishes in a blink. Then a backfill job runs it against 200,000 IDs, and: The database CPU pins at 100%, or too many clients already floods the logs Other endpoints on the same service start timing out The third-party API starts returning 429 Too Many Requests The process runs out of memory, or dies with EMFILE: too many open files Promise.all didn't do anything wrong. It did exactly what you asked. The problem is that you asked for unlimited concurrency , and you may not have realized it.

articles.title: Evaluating DeepSeek models broke three assumptions my rubric was built on
articles.excerpt: I started evaluating DeepSeek models the lazy way. The API speaks the same /v1/chat/completions shape as OpenAI, so I swapped the base_url, pointed my existing eval suite at R1, and waited for a score…
articles.body: I started evaluating DeepSeek models the lazy way. The API speaks the same /v1/chat/completions shape as OpenAI, so I swapped the base_url , pointed my existing eval suite at R1, and waited for a score. I got one, and it told me almost nothing. That suite was written for a closed model. It scored the final answer only, in one language, against one build of the weights. DeepSeek is cheap and the reasoning is strong. Neither fact tells you whether it can replace the model you run today, and three gaps in my rubric showed up before anything else did. Evaluating DeepSeek R1 means scoring the trace too R1 returns a reasoning_content field next to the final content . You can read it, store it, and score it. My rubric ignored it.

Google appears to be aware of the complaints but hasn’t publicly acknowledged a widespread issue, and there’s no confirmed fix yet. Apart from offering one of the best software experiences in the Android smartphone ecosystem, Google’s Pixel line is also known for its impressive camera capabilities . This isn’t a brand new issue, but it is resurfacing now.

articles.title: Track Amazon Best Sellers in 17 country stores with Python
articles.excerpt: If you're monitoring e-commerce trends, running a brand, or feeding a shopping assistant, you probably want what's selling on Amazon right now — not next week, and not just in the US. Amazon publishes…
articles.body: If you're monitoring e-commerce trends, running a brand, or feeding a shopping assistant, you probably want what's selling on Amazon right now — not next week, and not just in the US. Amazon publishes the Best Sellers and Hot New Releases charts for every category, in 17 country stores , updated every hour. Scraping those pages is cheap and doesn't need a login — this post shows how to do it from Python in three ways: today's top sellers, a cross-marketplace comparison, and a daily tracker that logs rank + price changes into SQLite. Code is in github.com/huynhtanan/amazon-bestsellers-tracker (MIT). Disclosure: I built the Apify scraper this uses; it's pay-per-result at $1 per 1,000 products , and new Apify accounts get free monthly credit that covers tens of thousands of items.
articles.author: huynhtanan

articles.title: calc-size() and round() stop your background pattern getting chopped at the bottom
articles.excerpt: Some ugliness only ever shows up on the last row of a tiled background. The pattern repeats perfectly, the content stops wherever the content stops, and the bottom row of tiles gets sliced in half lik…
articles.body: Some ugliness only ever shows up on the last row of a tiled background. The pattern repeats perfectly, the content stops wherever the content stops, and the bottom row of tiles gets sliced in half like a sprite with a broken hitbox. Everyone has shipped it. Most of us shipped it and then just stopped looking at the bottom of that section. Ahmad Shadeed ran into exactly this on a section whose pattern repeats on both axes. His write-up on ishadeed.com, published October 15, goes from the quick fix to a better one. The better one combines calc-size() with round() , and it's the kind of small, smart CSS move I want to see more of.

articles.title: pdfkit says "No wkhtmltopdf executable found" on Debian 13: HTML to PDF without the binary
articles.excerpt: If you rebuilt a Python image on python:3.13-slim recently and your invoice or report PDFs stopped, this is probably the error: OSError: No wkhtmltopdf executable found pdfkit (about 3 million downloa…
articles.body: If you rebuilt a Python image on python:3.13-slim recently and your invoice or report PDFs stopped, this is probably the error: OSError: No wkhtmltopdf executable found pdfkit (about 3 million downloads a month on PyPI) and imgkit are thin wrappers around the wkhtmltopdf binary. That binary's repository was archived after its last push in November 2022, and Debian removed the package from testing on 2025-02-05. Debian 13 is the base of the current python:3.13-slim image, so apt-get install wkhtmltopdf finds nothing. We checked this on Debian 13 on 2026-10-12 with pdfkit 1.0.0: pdfkit.from_url() stopped at the error above, and imgkit stopped at "No wkhtmltoimage executable found". Can't I just install the old .deb? You can.

articles.excerpt: "Just like here on Earth, Mars helicopters can cover distance quickly and can go places that might be impossible to reach by ground."
articles.body: NASA is accelerating the development of three helicopters that will be deployed into the sky above Mars after a voyage aboard NASA's Space Reactor‑1 Freedom spacecraft. Slated for launch in 2028, SR-1 Freedom is the first fission nuclear-powered interplanetary spacecraft and is assigned the duty of dropping off the SkyFall entry capsule loaded with the trio of aerial vehicles at the Red Planet. SR-1's trajectory will deliver the SkyFall helicopters in Mars' northern hemisphere during the planet's spring season to avoid dust storms . SkyFall is based on the success of the first aerial craft to float about the Red Planet , Ingenuity , which flew over 70 missions at Jezero Crater before it finally broke a rotor . It was designed to fly five.

articles.title: Beat light pollution with these six portable telescopes
articles.excerpt: Sick of skyglow spoiling your stargazing? These six telescopes are portable enough that you can easily pack them away and seek out darker skies.
articles.body: Light pollution is the astronomer's biggest enemy, especially if you're gazing into deep space. And while some of the best telescopes can make a difference, there's no way to eliminate it. That's why, if you want to observe the cosmos without obstruction, you need to seek out darker skies, get a smart telescope or combine the two. You don't have to book a flight to a dark sky reserve ; just traveling away from suburbia can be enough. That's where portable telescopes come in. Set one up in a field, for example, and you'll get a vastly improved view of the cosmos. Galaxies, nebulas and other deep space objects become more detailed when they're not washed out by skyglow.

articles.title: Anthropic warns small AI models could self-replicate through IoT devices
articles.excerpt: "Small weight-based replicators" could usher in a new generation of computer worms.
articles.body: AI company Anthropic is warning that advances in small AI models could soon usher in a new era of self-replicating malware that’s capable of infecting smart fridges, vacuum cleaners, and a wide range of other Internet of Things devices and is more resistant to takedown. By next year, smaller AI models may be able to autonomously self-replicate on all kinds of IoT devices, the company said. Eventually, the capability could enable computer worms, which propagate without requiring human interaction and are capable of infecting unfamiliar IoT devices. An experiment the company performed recently revealed significant challenges in bringing such an AI malware replicator to fruition, so the finding is necessarily tempered.
